_meta.title: Common Filipino dishes, nutrient values per 100 g edible portion
_meta.source: DOST-FNRI Philippine Food Composition Tables Online Database (PhilFCT), Release 1 December 2019
_meta.source_shape: Single unauthenticated HTML page, 17,444,645 bytes, HTTP 200, one <tr> plus one hidden Bootstrap modal per food; 1,542 distinct food entries parsed, matching the count recorded in docs/research/filipino-dish-values.md.
_meta.basis: Per 100 g edible portion (E.P.), the same basis FoodData Central uses.
_meta.licence: Philippine government works carry no copyright under RA 8293 section 176.1, so this non-commercial demonstration needs no approval from FNRI. The same section requires PRIOR APPROVAL of the originating agency for exploitation of the work FOR PROFIT, and FNRI may impose royalties as a condition. Before NutriGraph is used commercially, get FNRI's written position on these figures. Attribute DOST-FNRI PhilFCT wherever they are shown.

value_kind.direct: The PhilFCT entry is the dish itself.
value_kind.proxy: The PhilFCT entry stands in for the dish and is something else — usually a canned or commercial product, or a differently-cooked form. source_note states exactly what it is. Never present a proxy row as the home-cooked dish.
value_kind.calculated: PhilFCT holds no entry for the dish. The row is computed from component foods; the calculation object records components, PhilFCT Food IDs, gram weights and the arithmetic so a checker can recompute it.

_meta.calculated_row_assumption: No evaporation assumed. Water added during cooking is counted in the dish weight, so energy and nutrients per 100 g are likely understated rather than overstated. The component gram weights and the added-water figures on calculated rows are DECLARED, not sourced: FNRI publishes no recipe weights and no yield factors for any dish, and docs/research/filipino-dish-values.md section 4 records that even the Pinggang Pinoy serving grams could not be sourced. Every NUTRIENT number in this file, on every row, is transcribed from PhilFCT. No figure anywhere has been adjusted to compensate for the assumption.
_meta.nulls: fibre_g and sodium_mg are null wherever PhilFCT prints '-'. Never zero, never estimated. The 1997 base tables carried no fibre, sugar or sodium at all; the later indirect-method retrofit reached only about 1,246 items for fibre and 1,298 for sodium out of roughly 1,600.

dishes.name: Sinigang na baboy

calculation.method: Recipe calculation. For each component: contribution = PhilFCT per-100 g value * grams / 100. The contributions are summed and divided by the finished dish weight, then multiplied by 100. Finished dish weight = sum of component grams + water added. A column is null when any component's PhilFCT panel prints '-' for it; nothing is estimated to fill a gap.
calculation.assumption: No evaporation assumed. Water added during cooking is counted in the dish weight, so energy and nutrients per 100 g are likely understated rather than overstated.
calculation.recipe_weights_note: The component gram weights and the added-water figure are declared here, NOT taken from FNRI. PhilFCT publishes no recipe weights and no yield factors for any dish. Every NUTRIENT number below is transcribed from PhilFCT.

Every component nutrient value is transcribed from PhilFCT (https://i.fnri.dost.gov.ph/fct/library/search_item, fetched 2026-08-06); the component gram weights are declared, not sourced — FNRI publishes none. No evaporation assumed. Water added during cooking is counted in the dish weight, so energy and nutrients per 100 g are likely understated rather than overstated. No mayonnaise or egg is modelled. See the calculation object for components, PhilFCT Food IDs, grams and the arithmetic.

dishes.source_note: CALCULATED: PhilFCT holds no entry for chicken inasal under any name searched in the full 1542-item dataset, so this row is computed from component foods. Every component nutrient value is transcribed from PhilFCT (https://i.fnri.dost.gov.ph/fct/library/search_item, fetched 2026-08-06); the component gram weights are declared, not sourced — FNRI publishes none. No evaporation assumed. Water added during cooking is counted in the dish weight, so energy and nutrients per 100 g are likely understated rather than overstated. The chicken component is a RAW weight because PhilFCT holds no grilled-chicken entry, and grilling drives off a large share of that water. Annatto basting oil is not modelled. Of the six calculated rows this one and sisig carry the least added water, but this one carries the largest un-modelled cooking loss. See the calculation object for components, PhilFCT Food IDs, grams and the arithmetic.
